en.headline: MTR to pay government HK$2.25 billion over rail delay
en.dek: The one-off settlement covers the late high-speed rail link; both sides agreed not to pursue further claims on the Sha Tin to Central Link.
body: The government and the MTR Corporation have reached a settlement on delays to the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link's Hong Kong section and the Sha Tin to Central Link. Under the arrangement announced on Friday, the rail company will pay the government HK$2.25 billion for construction-stage delays on the high-speed line.

On the Sha Tin to Central Link, the two sides agreed not to pursue further claims against each other over project delays. The Transport and Logistics Bureau said the MTR Corporation had already borne about HK$2.8 billion in extra project-management costs for the whole scheme and extra spending linked to quality issues at the Hung Hom station extension. The bureau said the settlement had taken the company's responsibility for both delays into account.

A bureau spokesman said officials and the company had worked through large amounts of material under the dispute process set out in the entrustment agreements, drawing on independent engineering and legal advice, before reaching a consensus. The spokesman said lessons from both projects had been written into tighter governance, monitoring and cost-control arrangements, and applied to lines now under way, including Kwu Tung station, the Tung Chung Line extension, Oyster Bay station, the Tuen Mun South extension, Hung Shui Kiu station and the Northern Link.

Both railways were funded and owned by the government and entrusted to the MTR Corporation for design, construction, testing and operation. The high-speed section, begun in 2010 and originally due in August 2015, opened in September 2018 after a 2015 supplemental agreement capped the estimate at HK$84.42 billion. The Sha Tin to Central Link, begun in 2012, saw the full Tuen Ma Line open in June 2021 and the cross-harbour section in May 2022, with the estimate rising from HK$79.82 billion to HK$90.73 billion.

zh.headline: 港鐵就高鐵延誤向政府支付22.5億元
zh.dek: 政府與港鐵周五達成解決安排，沙中綫則因公司已承擔約28億元額外開支，雙方同意互不追討。
body: 政府周五與香港鐵路有限公司就廣深港高速鐵路香港段及沙田至中環綫工程延誤達成解決安排。就高鐵香港段建造階段的延誤，港鐵公司將向政府支付22.5億港元。
沙中綫方面，雙方同意就工程延誤不作互相追討。運輸及物流局表示，港鐵過去已主動承擔整個項目的額外項目管理費用，以及紅磡站擴建工程質量事件的相關額外開支，合共約28億港元。局方指，解決安排已考慮港鐵就兩項工程延誤的責任。
運輸及物流局發言人說，在委託協議訂明的爭議解決方式下，雙方整理及分析大量資料，並參考獨立的工程及法律意見，經過多輪商討後達成共識。發言人又說，兩項延誤後已加強鐵路工程的管治、監察和成本控制，並應用於現正推展的項目，包括古洞站、東涌綫延綫、小蠔灣站、屯門南延綫、洪水橋站及北環綫。根據新項目協議，港鐵須承擔相關建造及營運風險，包括超支。
兩條鐵路均由政府撥款興建及擁有，委託港鐵負責設計、建造、測試和營運。高鐵香港段於2010年動工，原定2015年8月通車，其後補充協議把竣工時間延至2018年第三季，造價估算由650億元增至844.2億元並封頂，2018年9月啟用。沙中綫於2012年動工，屯馬綫全綫2021年6月開通，過海段2022年5月啟用，造價估算由798.2億元增至907.3億元。
